import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_0.csv"
source_1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_1.csv"
source_2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_2.csv"
source_3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_3.csv"
source_4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_4.csv"
source_5_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_5.csv"
source_6_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_6.csv"
source_7_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/training_7.csv"

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_0_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_1_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_2_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'counts']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_3_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'counts']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_4_path, index_col=0)  # ['boro', 'zipcode']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_5_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'indicator', 'counts']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_6_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
df7 = pd.read_csv(source_7_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']

# Step 1: Rename 'businesses' and 'counts' columns in df0, df1, df6, df7 to match target columns
# Target columns related to businesses and counts:
# businesses_x, counts_x  <- from Source 7 (Sidewalk Cafe)
# businesses_y, counts_y  <- from Source 1 (Pawnbroker)
# businesses_x_5, counts_x_6 <- from Source 6 (Debt Collection Agency)
# businesses_y_7, counts_y_8 <- from Source 0 (Cigarette Retail Dealer)

# Rename df7 (Sidewalk Cafe) -> businesses_x, counts_x
df7_renamed = df7.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_x', 'counts': 'counts_x'})

# Rename df1 (Pawnbroker) -> businesses_y, counts_y
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_y', 'counts': 'counts_y'})

# Rename df6 (Debt Collection Agency) -> businesses_x_5, counts_x_6
df6_renamed = df6.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_x_5', 'counts': 'counts_x_6'})

# Rename df0 (Cigarette Retail Dealer) -> businesses_y_7, counts_y_8
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={'businesses': 'businesses_y_7', 'counts': 'counts_y_8'})

# Step 2: Merge these four business-related dataframes on 'zipcode'
# Start merging stepwise to keep code clear

# Merge df7_renamed and df1_renamed on 'zipcode'
df_biz_1 = pd.merge(df7_renamed, df1_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer')

# Merge with df6_renamed
df_biz_2 = pd.merge(df_biz_1, df6_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer')

# Merge with df0_renamed
df_biz_all = pd.merge(df_biz_2, df0_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer')

# Step 3: Merge counts columns from df2 and df3
# df2: ['zipcode', 'counts'] -> counts_x_10
# df3: ['zipcode', 'counts'] -> counts_y_11
df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={'counts': 'counts_x_10'})
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={'counts': 'counts_y_11'})

df_counts = pd.merge(df2_renamed, df3_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer')

# Step 4: Merge df4 (boro info) on 'zipcode'
# df4: ['boro', 'zipcode']
# Merge with df_biz_all first (businesses info)
df_biz_boro = pd.merge(df_biz_all, df4, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Step 5: Merge df5 (indicator and counts)
# df5: ['zipcode', 'indicator', 'counts']
df_final = pd.merge(df_biz_boro, df5, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Step 6: Final merge with counts from df_counts (counts_x_10, counts_y_11)
df_final = pd.merge(df_final, df_counts, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Step 7: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly:
# ['zipcode': integer,
#  'businesses_x': string,
#  'counts_x': integer,
#  'businesses_y': string,
#  'counts_y': integer,
#  'businesses_x_5': string,
#  'counts_x_6': integer,
#  'businesses_y_7': string,
#  'counts_y_8': integer,
#  'boro': string,
#  'counts_x_10': integer,
#  'counts_y_11': integer,
#  'indicator': string,
#  'counts': integer]

# Ensure all columns exist in df_final, if missing fill with NaN or appropriate default
expected_columns = [
    'zipcode',
    'businesses_x',
    'counts_x',
    'businesses_y',
    'counts_y',
    'businesses_x_5',
    'counts_x_6',
    'businesses_y_7',
    'counts_y_8',
    'boro',
    'counts_x_10',
    'counts_y_11',
    'indicator',
    'counts'
]

for col in expected_columns:
    if col not in df_final.columns:
        df_final[col] = pd.NA

# Convert zipcode to integer (some zipcodes might be missing, so use Int64 dtype to allow NA)
df_final['zipcode'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['zipcode'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Convert counts columns to integer (Int64 to allow NA)
counts_columns = [
    'counts_x', 'counts_y', 'counts_x_6', 'counts_y_8',
    'counts_x_10', 'counts_y_11', 'counts'
]
for col in counts_columns:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Reorder columns
df_final = df_final[expected_columns]

# Step 8: Sort by zipcode ascending for neatness (optional)
df_final = df_final.sort_values(by='zipcode')

# Step 9: Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_96/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
